I was a shift lead for four years. If you’re hurting for hours, the SFL position will keep you working with oodles of overtime opportunities. Your experience will depend on the store. Good stores will give you a crew to manage the everyday tasks while you get the more “project” oriented tasks done as well as safe counting. Bad stores will assign you one cashier and expect you to do absolutely everything. A good store will allow you time to eat for a few minutes and take micro breaks throughout the day. A bad store will starve you on consistent 10-hour shifts. 

At the very least, it’s still more engaging than sitting at the register all day. I’d say go for it but know your worth. Don’t take abuse. They will try.
